note: SUPPLEMENTARY predicate -- NOT the symptom of issue 4763, and its bisect history must not be read as the issue's history. It detects the OPPOSITE polarity: the OLD, pre-fix sizing of the fourth cbuffer in repro.hlsl, where a Buffer<float4> member consumed 16 bytes of constant-buffer space and pushed 'myInt' to offset 16 (cbuffer size 20). Current builds charge a Buffer<T> member 0 bytes and put myInt at offset 0 (size 4), which is the layout the reporter annotated as correct. A match here therefore means 'this release still has the old Buffer<T> sizing'; a no-match means 'this release has the fix' (or could not be measured -- clause 2 is the same SELF-TEST as match-layout.json, and clause 1 proves the compile finished, so an unmeasurable release fails those too). Purpose: to date, by measurement rather than by code-reading, the point at which the 'resources do not count towards cbuffer size' rule started being applied to Buffer<T>. Source reading says that is e6ba792e2 (2021-05-26, #3801), which added the rule at CGHLSLMS.cpp AddTypeAnnotation with the condition '!IsHLSLStructuredBufferType(Ty) && IsHLSLResourceType(Ty)' -- i.e. it deliberately excluded StructuredBuffer<T>, which is exactly the case the issue reports. This predicate exists to confirm that the same class of layout bug was fixed for one resource kind and left in place for the other.
